about: The ready-made pieces the designer offers: for each drawing whose movement fairy-chess tradition (or the drawing's own words) settles, the piece that moves that way, picked whole -- drawing, name and moves -- and editable after. docs/plan-pieces-moves.md section 1 is the reading of each; tests/test_ready_pieces.py holds every entry to it and compiles it. A piece carries no squares and names no other piece. 'rules' is a rule of the whole game the piece needs, which the designer offers to write, '@self' standing for the piece's own letter and '@royals' for the draft's royal pieces; 'note' is what the tradition adds that is left to the designer.

alfil.name: alfil
alfil.description: Jumps exactly two squares diagonally, over anything in between. It is the elephant of shatranj, the old Persian chess, and the bishop's ancestor.

amazon.name: amazon
amazon.description: Moves as a queen or jumps as a knight, the strongest of the classic invented pieces. Some old versions of chess gave the queen this power.

anchor.name: anchor
anchor.reading: a piece that never moves (its words: immobile, stuck, fixed)
anchor.description: Never moves. It blocks lines and can be jumped over, and is taken as any piece is.
anchor.note: It never moves: it blocks lines and screens hops, and is taken as any piece is.

antelope.name: antelope
antelope.description: Jumps three squares one way and four the other, a knight's jump stretched long. One of the classic invented chess pieces.

archbishop.name: archbishop
archbishop.description: Moves as a bishop or jumps as a knight. It comes from Capablanca's chess, played on a wider board.

arrow.name: archer
arrow.reading: an archer (its words: archer, shooter): a bishop whose every capture is a shot, Rifle chess's capture given to one piece
arrow.description: Moves like a bishop, any distance diagonally. With the game's shooting rule on, it takes by shooting, staying where it is, as every piece does in Rifle chess.
arrow.rules_say: It shoots only under rules.strike, a rule of the whole game: its captures take the target and leave it where it stood. Without that rule it is a plain bishop.

berolina.name: berolina pawn
berolina.reading: moves diagonally forward, captures straight forward (Berolina, E. Nebermann 1926)
berolina.description: Moves one square diagonally forward, two from its starting row, and takes one square straight forward: a pawn turned inside out. It comes from Berolina chess, 1926.
berolina.note: It promotes on the far rank only if the game says so: rules.promotion, which names what it may become.

bishop.name: bishop
bishop.description: Moves any distance diagonally until something is in the way. The bishop of chess.

bison.name: bison
bison.description: Jumps three squares one way and one or two the other, the camel's and the zebra's jumps together. An invented chess piece.

bolt.name: lightning
bolt.reading: the crooked bishop (its words: zigzag; Betza's boyscout, XBetza zB): diagonal steps turning one way and back, along a rank or a file
bolt.description: Moves any number of diagonal steps that zigzag back and forth, so its path runs along a row or a column. It is Ralph Betza's crooked bishop, shaped like its lightning drawing.

bomb.name: bomb
bomb.reading: Stratego's bomb, one shot: it never moves, and whatever takes it is destroyed with it
bomb.description: Never moves, and with the game's exploding rule on, whatever takes it is destroyed with it. It comes from the board game Stratego.
bomb.rules_say: Taking it destroys the taker too only under rules.explode_on_capture, a rule of the whole game. Without that rule it is a plain piece that never moves.

camel.name: camel
camel.description: Jumps three squares one way and one the other, a longer knight's jump. It comes from Tamerlane chess, a large medieval variant.

centaur.name: centaur
centaur.description: Steps one square in any direction, like a king, or jumps as a knight. An invented chess piece.

champion.name: champion
champion.description: Steps one square straight, or jumps two squares straight or diagonally. It comes from Omega chess.

chancellor.name: chancellor
chancellor.description: Moves as a rook or jumps as a knight. It comes from Capablanca's chess, played on a wider board.

commoner.name: commoner
commoner.reading: a king that is not royal
commoner.description: Steps one square in any direction, like a king, but losing it does not lose the game. An invented chess piece.

crown.name: flag
crown.reading: Stratego's flag: a royal that never moves
crown.description: Never moves, and the game is about not losing it, so it must be defended where it stands. It is the flag of the board game Stratego.
crown.note: Under win by royal capture taking it wins at once. Under checkmate a check on it can only be met by taking or blocking the checker, since it cannot step away.

crowned-bishop.name: dragon horse
crowned-bishop.description: Moves as a bishop, or steps one square straight. It is the dragon horse of shogi, Japanese chess, a promoted bishop.

crowned-rook.name: dragon king
crowned-rook.description: Moves as a rook, or steps one square diagonally. It is the dragon king of shogi, Japanese chess, a promoted rook.

dabbaba.name: dabbaba
dabbaba.description: Jumps exactly two squares forward, back or sideways, over anything in between. Its name, an old siege engine, comes from medieval Arabic chess.

dragon.name: dragon
dragon.description: Moves either as a knight or as a pawn: a step forward, two from its starting row, and a diagonal step forward to take. A favourite of chess puzzle composers.
dragon.note: It promotes on the far rank only if the game says so: rules.promotion, which names what it may become.

emperor.name: emperor
emperor.description: Steps one square in any direction, and the game is about not losing it, as with a king. Its drawing has no settled tradition, so it moves as a king.

eye.name: watcher
eye.reading: a watcher (its words: sight): a king's step, and every enemy it sees within two squares is frozen
eye.description: Steps one square in any direction, and freezes every enemy piece it sees within two squares in a straight or diagonal line, so those cannot move. A watching piece its drawing suggests.

facing-pawn.name: pawn
facing-pawn.reading: this project's own piece, not the tradition's: the pawn of weathervane, a pawn that points, so its forward and its captures turn with the way it faces (archive/weathervane.json plays it)
facing-pawn.description: A pawn that points: it moves and takes as a pawn, but towards the way it faces, which can be any side. A piece made here, for the game weathervane.
facing-pawn.note: Which way each pawn faces is set per placement (setup.placements[].facing: forward, backward, left or right), or for all of them by facing.initial. It promotes only if rules.promotion says so.

fad.name: fad
fad.description: Steps one square diagonally, or jumps two squares diagonally or two straight. An invented chess piece that reaches every nearby square of its own colour.

ferz.name: ferz
ferz.description: Steps one square diagonally. It is the counsellor of shatranj, the old Persian chess, and the queen's weak ancestor.

frog.name: frog
frog.description: Steps one square diagonally, or jumps exactly three squares straight. An invented chess piece.

ghost.name: ghost
ghost.reading: a queen that passes through (its words): every queen-line square up to seven away, as a leap
ghost.description: Jumps up to seven squares in any straight or diagonal line, passing through whatever is in between. A queen that goes through walls, as its drawing suggests.

giraffe.name: giraffe
giraffe.description: Jumps four squares one way and one the other, a very long knight's jump. An invented chess piece.

grasshopper.name: grasshopper
grasshopper.reading: a queen-line hop, landing just past the screen (Dawson)
grasshopper.description: Moves along any straight or diagonal line only by jumping over one piece, of either side, landing on the square just past it. Invented by the puzzle composer Thomas Dawson.

hourglass.name: hourglass
hourglass.reading: a timer (its words): a queen that rests two turns after it moves
hourglass.description: Moves as a queen, but after each move it must rest for its player's next two turns. A piece that keeps time, as its drawing suggests.

inverted-king.name: king
inverted-king.reading: a royal king (no canonical move of its own)
inverted-king.description: Steps one square in any direction, and the game is about not losing it. An upside-down king that moves as a king, since no tradition gives it a move of its own.

inverted-queen.name: grasshopper
inverted-queen.reading: the grasshopper (problemist convention: an upside-down queen)
inverted-queen.description: An upside-down queen is how puzzle books draw the grasshopper: it moves along any line only by jumping over one piece, landing just past it.

king.name: king
king.description: Steps one square in any direction, and the game is about not losing it. The king of chess.

kirin.name: kirin
kirin.description: Steps one square diagonally, or jumps two squares straight. It comes from chu shogi, a large Japanese chess.

knight.name: knight
knight.description: Jumps two squares one way and one the other, an L shape, over anything in between. The knight of chess.

man.name: man
man.reading: a king that is not royal (Betza's man)
man.description: Steps one square in any direction, like a king, but losing it does not lose the game. An invented chess piece.

moon.name: wizard
moon.description: Steps one square diagonally, or jumps three squares one way and one the other. It is the wizard of Omega chess.

nightrider.name: nightrider
nightrider.description: Makes any number of knight's jumps in a row in one direction, stopped by a piece on a square it would land on. Invented by Thomas Dawson in 1925.

paper.name: paper
paper.reading: rock-paper-scissors: a king's step, and it takes only the rock
paper.description: Steps one square in any direction. In a rock, paper and scissors set it takes only the rock, which you can set once all three are in.
paper.note: In rock-paper-scissors it takes only the rock. What it may take names other pieces, so it is left for you: once all three are in, set what each may capture, under more about this piece.

pawn.name: pawn
pawn.description: Moves one square forward, two from its starting row, and takes one square diagonally forward. The pawn of chess.
pawn.note: It promotes on the far rank only if the game says so: rules.promotion, which names what it may become. Taking in passing is rules.en_passant.

phoenix.name: phoenix
phoenix.description: Steps one square straight, or jumps two squares diagonally. It comes from chu shogi, a large Japanese chess.

prince.name: prince
prince.reading: a second royal that moves as a king (Tamerlane's prince)
prince.description: Steps one square in any direction, and the game is about not losing it, a second such piece beside the king. It comes from Tamerlane chess, a large medieval variant.
prince.note: A second royal: a game where a side holds two is won by royal capture (rules.win), and the check says so if it is not.

queen.name: queen
queen.description: Moves any distance in any straight or diagonal line until something is in the way. The queen of chess.

queen-star.name: super queen
queen-star.reading: queen and knight (its words: super queen)
queen-star.description: Moves as a queen or jumps as a knight, so it reaches more squares than any chess piece. An invented chess piece.

ring-rider.name: ring
ring-rider.reading: a circular rider (its words: circle, orbit, loop): one-square steps turning an eighth each time, round a small octagon
ring-rider.description: Steps one square at a time, turning one direction round with every step, so its path curves round a small circle. A circling piece its drawing suggests.

rock.name: rock
rock.reading: rock-paper-scissors: a king's step, and it takes only the scissors
rock.description: Steps one square in any direction. In a rock, paper and scissors set it takes only the scissors, which you can set once all three are in.
rock.note: In rock-paper-scissors it takes only the scissors. What it may take names other pieces, so it is left for you: once all three are in, set what each may capture, under more about this piece.

rook.name: rook
rook.description: Moves any distance forward, back or sideways until something is in the way. The rook of chess.

rook-diamond.name: rook and alfil
rook-diamond.description: Moves as a rook, or jumps exactly two squares diagonally. An invented chess piece.

rose.name: rose
rose.reading: the circular knight rider: knight steps turning an eighth each time, round an octagon (Parlett; XBetza qN)
rose.description: Makes knight's jumps one after another, each turning one direction round, so its path circles round an octagon. A classic invented chess piece.

royal-knight.name: royal knight
royal-knight.description: Jumps as a knight, and the game is about not losing it. It comes from Knightmate, where the king and the knights trade places.

saltire-rider.name: saltire
saltire-rider.description: Moves any distance diagonally until something is in the way, as a bishop does. Named for the diagonal cross its drawing shows.

scissors.name: scissors
scissors.reading: rock-paper-scissors: a king's step, and it takes only the paper
scissors.description: Steps one square in any direction. In a rock, paper and scissors set it takes only the paper, which you can set once all three are in.
scissors.note: In rock-paper-scissors it takes only the paper. What it may take names other pieces, so it is left for you: once all three are in, set what each may capture, under more about this piece.

sergeant.name: sergeant
sergeant.reading: one step forward or diagonally forward, a double step from home (Betza)
sergeant.description: Moves or takes one square forward or diagonally forward, and may step two forward from its starting row. An invented chess piece, a stronger pawn.
sergeant.note: It promotes on the far rank only if the game says so: rules.promotion, which names what it may become.

shield-king.name: warden
shield-king.description: Steps one square in any direction, and the game is about not losing it, as with a king. Its drawing has no settled tradition, so it moves as a king.

ship.name: ship
ship.description: Jumps exactly two squares diagonally, over anything in between. It is the boat of chaturaji, an old four-player Indian chess.

shogi-bishop.name: bishop
shogi-bishop.reading: shogi's bishop, as rulesets/shogi.json plays it
shogi-bishop.description: Moves any distance diagonally until something is in the way. The bishop of shogi, Japanese chess.

shogi-gold.name: gold
shogi-gold.reading: shogi's gold, as rulesets/shogi.json plays it
shogi-gold.description: Steps one square forward, back, sideways or diagonally forward. The gold general of shogi, Japanese chess.

shogi-king.name: king
shogi-king.reading: shogi's king, as rulesets/shogi.json plays it
shogi-king.description: Steps one square in any direction, and the game is about not losing it. The king of shogi, Japanese chess.

shogi-knight.name: knight
shogi-knight.reading: shogi's knight, as rulesets/shogi.json plays it
shogi-knight.description: Jumps two squares forward and one to either side, and only forward. The knight of shogi, Japanese chess.

shogi-lance.name: lance
shogi-lance.reading: shogi's lance, as rulesets/shogi.json plays it
shogi-lance.description: Moves any distance straight forward until something is in the way, and never back. The lance of shogi, Japanese chess.

shogi-pawn.name: pawn
shogi-pawn.reading: shogi's pawn, as rulesets/shogi.json plays it
shogi-pawn.description: Moves and takes one square straight forward. The pawn of shogi, Japanese chess.

shogi-promoted-bishop.name: horse
shogi-promoted-bishop.reading: shogi's horse, as rulesets/shogi.json plays it
shogi-promoted-bishop.description: Moves as a bishop, or steps one square straight. In shogi, Japanese chess, it is what a bishop becomes when promoted.
shogi-promoted-bishop.note: In shogi it is what a piece becomes on promotion: rules.promotion and promoted_from say that, and name pieces of your game.

shogi-promoted-knight.name: promoted knight
shogi-promoted-knight.reading: shogi's promoted knight, as rulesets/shogi.json plays it
shogi-promoted-knight.description: Steps one square forward, back, sideways or diagonally forward, as a gold general does. In shogi, Japanese chess, it is what a knight becomes when promoted.
shogi-promoted-knight.note: In shogi it is what a piece becomes on promotion: rules.promotion and promoted_from say that, and name pieces of your game.

shogi-promoted-lance.name: promoted lance
shogi-promoted-lance.reading: shogi's promoted lance, as rulesets/shogi.json plays it
shogi-promoted-lance.description: Steps one square forward, back, sideways or diagonally forward, as a gold general does. In shogi, Japanese chess, it is what a lance becomes when promoted.
shogi-promoted-lance.note: In shogi it is what a piece becomes on promotion: rules.promotion and promoted_from say that, and name pieces of your game.

shogi-promoted-pawn.name: tokin
shogi-promoted-pawn.reading: shogi's tokin, as rulesets/shogi.json plays it
shogi-promoted-pawn.description: Steps one square forward, back, sideways or diagonally forward, as a gold general does. The tokin of shogi, Japanese chess: what a pawn becomes when promoted.
shogi-promoted-pawn.note: In shogi it is what a piece becomes on promotion: rules.promotion and promoted_from say that, and name pieces of your game.

shogi-promoted-rook.name: dragon
shogi-promoted-rook.reading: shogi's dragon, as rulesets/shogi.json plays it
shogi-promoted-rook.description: Moves as a rook, or steps one square diagonally. In shogi, Japanese chess, it is what a rook becomes when promoted.
shogi-promoted-rook.note: In shogi it is what a piece becomes on promotion: rules.promotion and promoted_from say that, and name pieces of your game.

shogi-promoted-silver.name: promoted silver
shogi-promoted-silver.reading: shogi's promoted silver, as rulesets/shogi.json plays it
shogi-promoted-silver.description: Steps one square forward, back, sideways or diagonally forward, as a gold general does. In shogi, Japanese chess, it is what a silver becomes when promoted.
shogi-promoted-silver.note: In shogi it is what a piece becomes on promotion: rules.promotion and promoted_from say that, and name pieces of your game.

shogi-rook.name: rook
shogi-rook.reading: shogi's rook, as rulesets/shogi.json plays it
shogi-rook.description: Moves any distance forward, back or sideways until something is in the way. The rook of shogi, Japanese chess.

shogi-silver.name: silver
shogi-silver.reading: shogi's silver, as rulesets/shogi.json plays it
shogi-silver.description: Steps one square diagonally in any direction, or one straight forward. The silver general of shogi, Japanese chess.

short-rook.name: short rook
short-rook.reading: a rook limited to four (Betza, the Remarkable Rookies)
short-rook.description: Moves up to four squares forward, back or sideways, stopped by anything in the way. A shortened rook from Ralph Betza's chess variants.

snowflake.name: snowflake
snowflake.reading: a slider six ways, on a hex board (its words: six ways)
snowflake.description: On a board of six-sided cells, moves any distance in any of the six directions until something is in the way. It is the rook of hexagonal chess.

soldier.name: soldier
soldier.reading: the xiangqi soldier: one step forward, and sideways too once across the river
soldier.description: Steps one square forward. In xiangqi, Chinese chess, it also steps sideways once across the river, which you can add.
soldier.note: Across the river it steps sideways too. The river is squares of your board, so it is left for you: add a sideways step (wazir, lateral) and give it the far half of the board as its region, under more about this move.

spear.name: lance
spear.reading: the western lance, a forward rider
spear.description: Moves any distance straight forward until something is in the way, and never back. A western cousin of the shogi lance.

squirrel.name: squirrel
squirrel.description: Jumps to any square exactly two away: two straight, two diagonally, or a knight's jump. An invented chess piece.

threeleaper.name: threeleaper
threeleaper.description: Jumps exactly three squares forward, back or sideways, over anything in between. An invented chess piece.

trident.name: trident
trident.reading: a three-way rider (its words): forward and both forward diagonals
trident.description: Moves any distance straight forward or diagonally forward, until something is in the way. A three-pronged piece its drawing suggests.

tripper.name: tripper
tripper.description: Jumps exactly three squares diagonally, over anything in between. An invented chess piece.

unicorn.name: unicorn
unicorn.description: Moves like a bishop, or makes any number of knight's jumps in a row in one direction. An invented chess piece.

waffle.name: waffle
waffle.description: Steps one square straight, or jumps two squares diagonally. An invented chess piece, the same as the phoenix under another name.

wazir.name: wazir
wazir.description: Steps one square forward, back or sideways. It comes from medieval Arabic chess, where it was the king's minister.

xiangqi-advisor.name: advisor
xiangqi-advisor.reading: xiangqi's advisor, as rulesets/xiangqi.json plays it
xiangqi-advisor.description: Steps one square diagonally. The advisor of xiangqi, Chinese chess, where it stays inside its palace, which you can add.
xiangqi-advisor.note: In xiangqi it stays in the palace. Those are squares of your board, so they are left for you: give it a region, under more about this piece.

xiangqi-cannon.name: cannon
xiangqi-cannon.reading: xiangqi's cannon, as rulesets/xiangqi.json plays it
xiangqi-cannon.description: Moves like a rook, but takes only by jumping over exactly one piece to land on the piece beyond. The cannon of xiangqi, Chinese chess.

xiangqi-chariot.name: chariot
xiangqi-chariot.reading: xiangqi's chariot, as rulesets/xiangqi.json plays it
xiangqi-chariot.description: Moves any distance forward, back or sideways until something is in the way. The chariot of xiangqi, Chinese chess, its rook.

xiangqi-elephant.name: elephant
xiangqi-elephant.reading: xiangqi's elephant, as rulesets/xiangqi.json plays it
xiangqi-elephant.description: Moves two squares diagonally, but not if the square between is occupied. The elephant of xiangqi, Chinese chess, where it stays on its own side of the river.
xiangqi-elephant.note: In xiangqi it stays in its own side of the river. Those are squares of your board, so they are left for you: give it a region, under more about this piece.

xiangqi-general.name: general
xiangqi-general.reading: xiangqi's general, as rulesets/xiangqi.json plays it
xiangqi-general.description: Steps one square forward, back or sideways, and the game is about not losing it. The general of xiangqi, Chinese chess, where it stays inside its palace.
xiangqi-general.note: In xiangqi it stays in the palace. Those are squares of your board, so they are left for you: give it a region, under more about this piece.

xiangqi-horse.name: horse
xiangqi-horse.reading: xiangqi's horse, as rulesets/xiangqi.json plays it
xiangqi-horse.description: Jumps as a knight, but is blocked by a piece on the square next to it in the direction it sets off. The horse of xiangqi, Chinese chess.

xiangqi-pictorial-advisor.name: advisor
xiangqi-pictorial-advisor.reading: xiangqi's advisor, as rulesets/xiangqi.json plays it
xiangqi-pictorial-advisor.description: Steps one square diagonally. The advisor of xiangqi, Chinese chess, where it stays inside its palace, which you can add.
xiangqi-pictorial-advisor.note: In xiangqi it stays in the palace. Those are squares of your board, so they are left for you: give it a region, under more about this piece.

xiangqi-pictorial-cannon.reading: xiangqi's cannon, as rulesets/xiangqi.json plays it
xiangqi-pictorial-cannon.description: Moves like a rook, but takes only by jumping over exactly one piece to land on the piece beyond. The cannon of xiangqi, Chinese chess.

xiangqi-pictorial-chariot.reading: xiangqi's chariot, as rulesets/xiangqi.json plays it
xiangqi-pictorial-chariot.description: Moves any distance forward, back or sideways until something is in the way. The chariot of xiangqi, Chinese chess, its rook.

xiangqi-pictorial-elephant.description: Moves two squares diagonally, but not if the square between is occupied. The elephant of xiangqi, Chinese chess, where it stays on its own side of the river.
xiangqi-pictorial-elephant.note: In xiangqi it stays in its own side of the river. Those are squares of your board, so they are left for you: give it a region, under more about this piece.

xiangqi-pictorial-general.reading: xiangqi's general, as rulesets/xiangqi.json plays it
xiangqi-pictorial-general.description: Steps one square forward, back or sideways, and the game is about not losing it. The general of xiangqi, Chinese chess, where it stays inside its palace.
xiangqi-pictorial-general.note: In xiangqi it stays in the palace. Those are squares of your board, so they are left for you: give it a region, under more about this piece.

xiangqi-pictorial-horse.name: horse
xiangqi-pictorial-horse.reading: xiangqi's horse, as rulesets/xiangqi.json plays it
xiangqi-pictorial-horse.description: Jumps as a knight, but is blocked by a piece on the square next to it in the direction it sets off. The horse of xiangqi, Chinese chess.

xiangqi-pictorial-soldier.reading: xiangqi's soldier, as rulesets/xiangqi.json plays it
xiangqi-pictorial-soldier.description: Steps one square forward. The soldier of xiangqi, Chinese chess, where it also steps sideways once across the river, which you can add.

xiangqi-soldier.reading: xiangqi's soldier, as rulesets/xiangqi.json plays it
xiangqi-soldier.description: Steps one square forward. The soldier of xiangqi, Chinese chess, where it also steps sideways once across the river, which you can add.

zebra.name: zebra
zebra.description: Jumps three squares one way and two the other, a stretched knight's jump. One of the classic invented chess pieces.
